title: Personal OKR weekly check-in - Week of 2026-03-08
content:
Week: 2026-03-08
Status: draft (quick personal notes / scratchpad for weekly sync)

Context:
- Role: Eng (serving runtime) - focusing on inference latency/regression prevention and rollout controls for Dedicated customers.
- High-level OKR alignment: O1 = Improve inference latency and predictability (esp p99), O2 = Reduce per-token cost for high-throughput workloads, O3 = Improve rollout safety for model variants.

Wins this week:
- Merged PR #785 (kv-cache warmup heuristic) - preliminary canary telemetry shows p95 improvement on small seq workloads.
- Ran manual eval across 3 customer workloads (search-rewrite, chat-short, summarization) and collected baseline metrics.
- Paired with SRE on canary rollback automation (added simple health-check stage).

Metrics snapshot (current vs target):
- O1 KR1: p99 latency for typical 2k-token reqs: baseline = 320ms, target = 288ms (-10%). Current (after canary): 305ms (~4.7% improvement).
- O1 KR2: cold-start rate under 200ms: baseline 62%, target 80%. Current 68% (still noisy for small bursts).
- O2 KR1: cost per 1M tokens (hosted model X-7B-quant): baseline $62 -> target $55. Current $60 (small wins from batching).

Progress vs Key Results (notes):
- KR1: good directional improvement from KV warmup; need broader traffic mix. Canary traffic so far limited to internal test-traffic.
- KR2: cold-start reduction requires instance reuse + quicker kernel init. Filing infra follow-up.
- Cost KR: batching configs gave ~3% unit savings; need caching + longer-lived KV sharing for bigger wins.

Experiments / what I ran:
- Canary A/B: baseline vs kv-warmup: p95 reduced by ~18ms on small seqs; p99 reduced ~15ms.
- Batch-size sweep (simulated): throughput up ~8% at batch=64 for chat-short workload, but tail latency regressed for tail sessions - need smarter batching policy per route.

Blockers / open questions:
- Telemetry: tracing for cold-starts is missing a couple of spans (kernel init). Filing JIRA-INF-342 to track. Need infra help to add kernel-init timers.
- Quota: can't run full 24h mixed-traffic eval due to infra quota; asked infra for temporary bump (Slack @sre-infra).
- Rollouts: want to add automated fallback to previous quantized parity model on regression - need product sign-off on RBAC rules.

Next week (concrete TODOs):
- Run expanded canary (50k reqs) across representative workloads (task: automation script + data set) - target: capture p99 distribution by route.
- Follow up on JIRA-INF-342 (add tracing spans) and pair with Evan on instrumentation.
- Prototype per-route batching policy (config + simple heuristic) and test on staging.
- Prepare short section for Friday WG: "latency improvements & outstanding risks" (2 slides).
- Personal learning: schedule two reading sessions (quantization internals) and a 1:1 with Maya to review rollout concerns.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider a light-weight client-side caching signal for repeated prefixes (might reduce first-10-token churn).
- Explore automatic heuristic: if route median seq_len < 128 -> favor lower batch size to reduce tail.
- Could expose a per-customer latency SLO hint so routing can favor lower-batch-config for strict customers.

Links / artifacts referenced:
- Confluence notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INF-128
- JIRA: JIRA-INF-342 (kernel-init tracing)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/785
- Slack: #eng-serving-runtime thread: slack.com/archives/C12345/p1710000000

Meeting asks / who to ping:
- Evan Li (instrumentation) - need help adding kernel-init spans.
- SRE (quota): request temporary infra bump for 24h evaluation.
- Product (Maya): quick thumbs-up on canary fallback policy before we widen traffic.

Quick retrospective (last 2 weeks):
- What went well: quicker turnaround on PRs, better pairing with SRE.
- Improvements: want earlier smoke tests pre-merge (CI) and clearer evaluation checklist so canary is less manual.

TODO (inline):
- [ ] Add evaluation automation job (script + dataset)
- [ ] Create short runbook for canary rollback
- [ ] Schedule 1:1 with Maya this week

End of note.
